Ambedkar, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, Kautilya's classical administrative-ethics ideals
Indian administrative-integrity role models used as case anchors: T.N. Seshan, E. Sreedharan

Western philosophers used as ethics-paper anchors: Plato, Aristotle, Socrates, Jeremy Bentham, J.S. Mill, Thomas Hobbes, John Locke, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, John Rawls, Immanuel Kant (categorical imperative applied to public service), Carol Gilligan, Jean-Paul Sartre, Hegel, Confucius, Rene Descartes, Karl Marx, Adam Smith, Thomas Aquinas, David Hume, Montesquieu, Friedrich Nietzsche
Administrative-management thinkers used as case anchors: Max Weber, Elton Mayo, Peter Drucker, Chester Barnard, Mary Parker Follett

Global moral/civic exemplars used as case anchors: Abraham Lincoln, Nelson Mandela, Martin Luther King, Aung San Suu Kyi, Dalai Lama, Mother Teresa, Albert Einstein, J.L. Nehru, Lee Kuan Yew, Henry Ford, Abdul Kalam, Muhammad Yunus, Wangari Maathai, Kofi Annan, Desmond Tutu, Elie Wiesel

Frequently cited quotation-anchors for ethics answer-writing: Gandhi's 'Seven Sins' and 'the weak can never forgive'; Socrates' 'an unexamined life is not worth living'; Nehru on awakening women as key to awakening the nation; Jefferson's 'honesty is the first chapter in the book of wisdom' (intellectual vs functional honesty); Warren Buffett's 'integrity, intelligence, energy' hiring framework; and comparable Lincoln/Gandhi/Tirukkural anchors

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Attitude: content, structure, function; its influence and relation with thought and behaviour; moral and political attitudes; social influence and persuasion.
micro_themes: Components of attitude: affective, cognitive, and behavioural components
Functions of attitude: adjustive, ego-defensive, value-expressive, and knowledge functions
Attitude-formation model, impact of beliefs and values, group and social influences, persuasion tactics and tools
Moral and political attitude formation; distinguishing 'attitude' from 'belief' and how cognitive dissonance affects internal alignment
Attitude-behaviour gap in civil-servant decision-making under political pressure; persuasion techniques in public communication and citizen behaviour-change campaigns

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: Aptitude and Foundational Values for Civil Service
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Aptitude and foundational values for Civil Service, integrity, impartiality and non-partisanship, objectivity, dedication to public service, empathy, tolerance and compassion towards the weaker-sections.
micro_themes: Essential aptitude for civil servants; foundational values of civil services: neutrality, anonymity, accountability, integrity, humility, adaptability, magnanimity, perseverance, impartiality/non-partisanship, tolerance and compassion for the weaker sections, and contribution to society
Empathy and compassion as values distinguishing a pro-poor administrator from a status-quoist one; consequences of political alignment by bureaucrats
Can an administrator succeed on aptitude alone, without integrity? — the integrity-vs-competence debate; impartiality maintenance under political transfer-posting pressures

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Emotional intelligence-concepts, and their utilities and application in administration and governance.
micro_themes: Theories associated with emotional intelligence and whether EI can be developed; components of emotional competence
The self-awareness cluster (understanding feelings, accurate self-assessment) and self-management cluster (managing internal states/impulses/resources)
The social-awareness cluster (reading people/groups accurately) and relationship-management cluster (inducing desirable responses in others)
Importance of EI at the workplace and in civil services; components of EI applied to conflict resolution and crisis-time administrative communication

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: Public/Civil Service Values and Ethics in Public Administration
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Status and problems; ethical concerns and dilemmas in government and private institutions; laws, rules, regulations and conscience as sources of ethical guidance; accountability and ethical governance; strengthening of ethical and moral values in governance; ethical issues in international relations and funding; corporate governance.
micro_themes: Ethical concerns/dilemmas in public and private institutions; laws/rules/regulations vs conscience as sources of ethical guidance; accountability and ethical-governance strengthening
Moral judgements in international relations; ethical relation in funding international relations and the concept of moral responsibility; ethics in the working of international organisations
Corporate governance: concept, models of Corporate Social Responsibility, World Bank steps for good corporate governance, and norms for corporate governance in India; concept of business ethics
Structural flaws in asset-disclosure regulations for public officials and their effectiveness against illegal wealth generation; whether public asset-declaration has improved governance
Judicial independence as a democratic prerequisite, and where judicial overreach threatens democratic balance
Conflict of interest: definition, actual vs potential conflicts, with illustrative examples; administrative value conflicts in maintaining political neutrality while processing sensitive files
Conscience vs conformity: whistleblowing dilemmas within rule-bound bureaucratic hierarchies (including the Edward Snowden case — legality vs moral obligation to inform the public)
Corporate ESG auditing: ethical constraints around corporate greenwashing and environmental-accounting metrics

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Concept of public service; Philosophical basis of governance and probity; Information sharing and transparency in government, Right to Information, Codes of Ethics, Codes of Conduct, Citizen’s Charters, Work culture, Quality of service delivery, Utilization of public funds, challenges of corruption.
micro_themes: Concept of public service and the philosophical basis of governance/probity; public servants as 'trustees' of public power and financial resources
'Constitutional morality': concept and how it is enforced in a democratic system; social auditing as more than financial verification — an instrument of ethical governance
Distinguishing a 'Code of Conduct' from a 'Code of Ethics'; code of conduct for ministers/legislators/civil servants/regulators/judiciary
Information sharing, transparency and Right to Information: importance of vigilant citizens, information-sharing/participation, flaws in RTI and improvement recommendations
Components of a Citizen's Charter and steps in its formulation; concept of work culture, the Indian approach to work, methods of improving work culture, and quality of service delivery
Accountability vs Responsibility: distinguishing the two with a suitable example; utilisation of public funds and problems in fund release/utilisation; parliamentary control on expenditure

Corruption in India: extent, dimension, and response; corruption as a social evil; probity in public life; exposing corruption via civil-society initiatives and the Whistleblower Act; tackling and controlling corruption via various institutional approaches

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Case Studies on above issues.
micro_themes: Euthanasia: social/ethical dimensions, arguments for and against
Surrogacy: ethical issues and the concept of ethical surrogacy
Ethics in sports: need for sportsmanship, doping, discrimination and sexual harassment, sport-as-business ethics
Media ethics: role of media, ethical issues faced by reporters, trial by media, media prejudice, ethical dilemmas of photo-journalists, digital-media ethics, paid news
Business ethics: principles, dimensions within organisations, business ethics and corporate governance, philanthropy-to-CSR journey, and implementation issues
Ethics related to economic sanctions: why sanctions are placed and the ethics of imposing them
Refugees and ethics: why migration occurs, the Syria case study, dilemmas of the refugee crisis, and steps needed
Ethical dilemmas of globalization: free trade, criticism of the global regime, and the way forward
Ethics of war: war theories and the evils of war
Environmental ethics: linkage between ethics and environment, relevant theories, and the role of the individual
Ethical issues in biotechnology: stem cells, cloning, designer babies
Animal ethics: research on animals, keeping animals as pets, cruelty against animals
Food adulteration and ethics; abortion (legal status in India, recent Supreme Court verdict, women's-health-vs-fetus dilemma, justification/argument-against, women's/father's rights)

Honour killing (why it is unethical, role of khap panchayats); marital rape (arguments for/against criminalization and the hurdles); child labour (children's rights, corporate role, solutions, consumer's role)
Treating juveniles as adults: juvenile-justice-system implications; ethics and old age (issues faced, importance of autonomy); ethics in public vs private relationships and their linkage

Case studies: public-service integrity & corruption dilemmas: welfare-scheme 'ghost beneficiary' fraud amid caste sensitivities, law-enforcement bribery from an illegal-mining network, superior's personal-gain conflict-of-interest request, tax officer's technical-vs-substantial-compliance discretion, food/drug-safety-regulator cover-up offer

Case studies: welfare-access & exclusion dilemmas: digital/biometric exclusion of a genuine welfare beneficiary, biometric-mandate exclusion of poor/labour children, eligibility-criteria strict-rule-vs-humane-exception dilemmas

Case studies: whistleblowing, disclosure & confidentiality dilemmas: whistleblower/suspect pleading humanitarian delay, workplace-harassment complaint with a confidentiality request, industrial-pollution complaint against a politically-connected employer

Case studies: development vs displacement/environment trade-offs: environmental clearance vs displacement/pollution trade-offs, court-ordered demolition vs livelihood/political pressure, factory-closure aftermath (unemployment vs environmental enforcement)

Case studies: public-safety & procurement dilemmas under pressure: infrastructure-safety cover-up under election-timeline pressure, defence-procurement L1-vs-clean-bidder dilemma, clinical-trial consent violations vs public-health urgency

Case studies: crisis & resource-allocation dilemmas: drought-relief tanker capture by a 'tanker mafia', disaster resource-allocation triage (elite vs marginalised site), law-and-order vs root-cause balancing (illicit liquor), government-doctor private-practice neglect with union-strike threat

Technology & AI ethics (case studies): drone ethics, AI ethics (in healthcare, creativity, human rights), technological ethics (facial recognition, crypto-mining, brain-computer interfaces), ethics in Digital Public Infrastructure, online-gaming/mining ethics

Governance & institutional ethics (case studies): ethics of elections, parliamentary-privilege ethics, judicial ethics (recusal, majoritarianism), political conflict-of-interest, paper-leak and examination-malpractice ethics

Public discourse & rights ethics (case studies): internet-shutdown ethics, free speech on social media, social-media influencing, moral policing, identity politics and gender justice, sex-workers'/LGBTQIA+ rights, reproductive rights, 'wokeism' debates
Health & bio-ethics (case studies): medical ethics (organ transplant, clinical trials), student suicides, stray-dog-management ethics

Labour & social-welfare ethics (case studies): manual-scavenging as societal ethics, labour/worker ethics (working hours), live-in-relationship ethics, food-service safety ethics, consumerism, individual social responsibility, nudge ethics

International & security ethics (case studies): ethics in international relations (trade, war, climate finance), arbitration ethics, peacekeeping and humanitarian intervention, ethics of grey-zone warfare
